To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a high-throughput screening platform to functionally characterize metagenomic libraries for plant polymer degrading activities and identified 374 clones from fosmid library of leaf litter that hydrolyze cellulose, hematicellulose, starch, chitin, protein and phosphate.

we developed a high throughput screening platform for function-based characterization and sequencing of metagenomic fosmid libraries and applied it to identify genes for carbohydrate-active enzymes involved in decomposition of plant polymers.
we have developed a new platform for high-throughput functional metagenomic analysis and used it to identify a diverse set of plant polymer decomposers in environmental metagenomic fosmid libraries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel high throughput platform for functional screening of metatranscriptomic libraries and its application to identify novel enzymes involved in plant polymer degradation in soil microbial communities.
the development and application of high-throughput screening methods for the characterization of metagenomic clones and their products.

the identification and functional characterization of novel plant polymer degrading enzymes from environmental metagenomes, using a combination of next-generation sequencing and high-throughput functional screens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional screening platform described in this paper is a valuable tool for identifying novel enzymes and linking them to specific microbial taxa in metagenomes.
the functional screening platform described here provides a powerful tool for linking metagenomic sequencing data and microbial community composition to specific metabolic traits.

the combination of functional screening and next-generation sequencing is the most powerful approach in identifying genes encoding for enzymes involved in plant biomass degradation from environmental samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this study demonstrates the feasibility of high-throughput functional characterization of plant polymer degrading activities in metagenomic clones and the utility of such a strategy in linking functional traits and community structure.
we developed and tested a high-throughput functional screen for metagenomic libraries and used it to characterize fosmid clones that hydrolyze plant polymers from decomposing leaf-litter.
we developed a platform for function-based mining of metageneomic libraries and demonstrated its application to the identification of plant polymer hydrolyzing enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of functional screening with next generation sequencing provides a unique opportunity to link microbial community composition with the functional traits of individual organisms.
the integration of functional screening and sequencing is a powerful approach for linking microbial function to community composition.

the combination of high-throughput functional assays with next generation sequencing can be used for rapid and efficient characterization of the functional roles of microbial communities in natural environments.
